final_answer: Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, while breadth-first search (BFS) explores all the neighbors at the current depth before moving to the next level. DFS is useful for problems where the solution is not deep in the graph, or when memory is limited. BFS is better for finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph. The choice depends on the specific problem requirements and constraints.
